gap: No result ChatGPT got states talk time, the battery figure for calls. The makers' talk times with ANC on reverse the headline battery order: Jabra Evolve3 85 is up to 21 h and Sony WH-1000XM6 is up to 24 h. Their music figures (55 h vs 30 h) point the other way, and those are what SoundGuys prints. Bose publishes no talk time, and Bose's own footnote gives 24 h of music at full noise cancelling against a 30 h headline.
standout_why: The cited SoundGuys work page (dated 2026-10-22, read 2026-11-14) gives Jabra Evolve3 85 as 'up to 55 h with ANC on' and Sony WH-1000XM6 as '30 h with ANC on', plus its own 37 h 14 min Sony test. All of these are music-playback figures, and the page gives no talk time for any pick. It already has the mic-count split (Sony: 12 total, 6-mic call array; Jabra: six), so mic counts are not new. The cited RTINGS phone-calls page returned only navigation to the fetcher, so I could not check whether it gives talk time. ChatGPT's answers give no battery numbers. Our current page gives talk time for only 2 of 6 rows: Space 2 Pro 20 h, and 21 to 26 h for the Evolve2 85, which is now superseded by the Evolve3 85 that ChatGPT showed.
decides: This confirms the Sony WH-1000XM6 as the all-round pick and removes battery as a reason to pay more for the Jabra. On a call with ANC on, Sony rates 24 h and Jabra 21 h, despite Jabra's 55 h vs 30 h music headline. On ANC-on talk time the Jabra is a draw at best. The case for it is still mic clarity (SoundGuys: 'sounded the clearest of the tested mics'), the Link 390 dongle and Teams/Zoom certification, not endurance. The table should have a 'talk time, ANC on' column, and the footnote should say that music hours overstate call hours by 6 h (Sony) to 34 h (Jabra).
